ei.title: How Three Product Versions Shape Consumer Choice
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.

questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon (A)[forgot / discovered] why there are often three versions of many (B)[industrial / consumer] goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been (C)[willing / reluctant] to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) discovered=발견했다, (B) consumer=소비자의, (C) willing=기꺼이 ~하려는
det.analysis:
✅ ① discovered — consumer — willing: 원문 일치. 필자는 왜 세 가지 버전이 있는지 알아냈고(discovered), 그것은 소비자(consumer) 제품이며, 사람들이 기꺼이(willing) 더 쓰려 했다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② forgot — consumer — willing: (A) forgot(잊었다)은 이유를 '알아냈다(discovered)'는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ discovered — industrial — willing: (B) industrial(산업의)은 '소비자(consumer)' 제품이라는 맥락과 다름
❌ ④ discovered — consumer — reluctant: (C) reluctant(꺼리는)는 '기꺼이(willing)' 돈을 쓴다는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: I soon discovered(곧 알아냈다) / consumer goods(소비자 제품) / willing to spend(기꺼이 쓰려는)

If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) compare=비교하다, (B) introduces=도입하다, (C) manipulated=조종당한
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignore — introduces — manipulated: (A) ignore(무시하다)는 두 모델을 '비교한다(compare)'는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② compare — removes — manipulated: (B) removes(없앤다)는 세 번째 모델을 '도입한다(introduces)'는 맥락과 반대
✅ ③ compare — introduces — manipulated: 원문 일치. 사람들은 모델을 비교하고(compare), 회사가 세 번째 모델을 도입하며(introduces), 소비자는 조종당한(manipulated) 줄 모른다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ compare — introduces — informed: (C) informed(정보를 잘 아는)는 '조종당한(manipulated)' 맥락과 반대
det.tip: compare the two models(두 모델을 비교하다) / introduces a third model(세 번째 모델을 도입하다) / have been manipulated(조종당해 왔다)

questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some (A)[expense / income]. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, (B)[costs / sales] of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the (C)[presence / absence] of the higher-priced item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) income=수입, (B) sales=판매량, (C) presence=존재
det.analysis:
❌ ① expense — sales — presence: (A) expense(지출)는 회사가 '수입(income)'을 잃는다는 맥락과 다름
❌ ② income — costs — presence: (B) costs(비용)는 두 번째 모델의 '판매량(sales)'이 오른다는 맥락과 다름
❌ ③ income — sales — absence: (C) absence(부재)는 더 비싼 품목의 '존재(presence)'에 조종당한다는 맥락과 반대
✅ ④ income — sales — presence: 원문 일치. 회사는 수입(income)을 잃고, 두 번째 모델의 판매량(sales)이 오르며, 더 비싼 품목의 존재(presence)에 소비자가 조종당한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: losing some income(수입을 잃다) / sales ... go up(판매량이 오르다) / the presence of the higher-priced item(더 비싼 품목의 존재)

det.korean: ② concealed(숨겼다) → discovered(알아냈다): 필자는 세 버전이 있는 이유를 '알아냈다'는 맥락

❌ ③ product — 원문 일치. 제품의 한 가지 버전이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ income — 원문 일치. 회사가 수입을 잃는다는 맥락에 적절

det.korean: ③ rewarded(보상받은) → manipulated(조종당한): 소비자는 더 비싼 품목의 존재에 '조종당한' 것
det.analysis:
✅ ① offers — 원문 일치. 회사가 두 가지 버전을 제공한다는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② introduces — 원문 일치. 세 번째 모델을 도입한다는 맥락에 적절

det.korean: ④ lower-priced(더 싼) → higher-priced(더 비싼): 소비자는 '더 비싼' 품목의 존재에 조종당함
det.analysis:
✅ ① consumer — 원문 일치. 소비자 제품이라는 맥락에 적절

✅ ③ least — 원문 일치. 중간 품목이 가장 싼 것보다 기능이 많다는 맥락에 적절

det.analysis:

✅ ② down: down(아래로/내려가다)은 up(위로/오르다)의 반의어로, 판매량이 '오른다(go up)'의 반대 ←정답
❌ ③ forward: forward(앞으로)는 상하 방향이 아님
❌ ④ over: over(위에/넘어)는 up의 반대가 아님
det.tip: sales go up(판매량이 오르다) ↔ go down(내려가다)

questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, so the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the <u>higher-priced</u> item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 higher-priced와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: higher-priced=더 비싼 → cheaper=더 싼 (반의어)
det.analysis:
❌ ① costlier: costlier(더 비싼)는 higher-priced와 유사한 의미
❌ ② pricier: pricier(더 비싼)는 higher-priced와 유사한 의미
✅ ③ cheaper: cheaper(더 싼)는 higher-priced(더 비싼)의 반의어 ←정답
❌ ④ premium: premium(고급의/비싼)은 higher-priced와 유사 계열
det.tip: higher-priced(더 비싼) ↔ cheaper(더 싼)

questions.passage:
(A) Many customers were willing to <u>spend</u> more money on the model with extra features.
(B) We decided to <u>spend</u> the entire weekend relaxing quietly at the beach.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 spend의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: spend: (A) (돈을) 쓰다 / (B) (시간을) 보내다
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) (돈을) 쓰다 — (B) (시간을) 보내다: (A)는 'spend more money'로 돈을 쓰다, (B)는 'spend the entire weekend'로 시간을 보내다의 뜻으로 다의어의 두 의미를 올바르게 연결 ←정답
❌ ② (A) (시간을) 보내다 — (B) (돈을) 쓰다: (A)의 spend는 money와 함께 쓰여 돈을 쓰다
❌ ③ (A) (돈을) 쓰다 — (B) (돈을) 쓰다: (B)는 weekend와 함께 쓰여 시간을 보내다
❌ ④ (A) 아끼다 — (B) 낭비하다: 두 문맥의 의미와 모두 어긋남
det.tip: spend money(돈을 쓰다) / spend time(시간을 보내다)

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a company or person that makes goods in large quantities, especially in a factory"

det.korean: manufacturer=제조업체 (공장에서 대량으로 제품을 만드는 회사나 사람)
det.analysis:
✅ ① manufacturer: manufacturer(제조업체)는 공장에서 대량으로 제품을 만드는 회사/사람으로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ② consumer: consumer(소비자)는 제품을 쓰는 사람으로, '만드는' 주체가 아님
❌ ③ customer: customer(고객)는 제품을 사는 사람으로 정의와 다름
❌ ④ retailer: retailer(소매업체)는 제품을 파는 상인으로, 대량 '제조'와 다름
det.tip: manufacturer = 제조업체. makes goods in large quantities(대량 제조)가 핵심

questions.passage: If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who __________ (buy) it might have been willing to spend more money. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 가정·과거 상황의 관계사절 동사: buy → 과거형 bought
det.analysis: 'people who __________ it'에서 관계대명사 who의 동사 자리이며, 뒤의 'might have been willing'(과거의 추측)과 호응하여 과거에 그것을 '산' 사람들을 가리키므로 과거형 bought가 적절. buy → bought
det.tip: people who bought it = 그것을 샀던 사람들 (과거형)

questions.passage: The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been __________ (manipulate) by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 현재완료 수동태 'have been + 과거분사': manipulate → manipulated
det.analysis: 'they have been __________ by ~'는 현재완료 수동태 'have been + 과거분사(p.p.)' 구조이다. 소비자는 '조종당하는' 대상이므로 수동태 과거분사 manipulated가 적절. manipulate → manipulated
det.tip: 현재완료 수동태: have been + p.p. = ~당해 왔다. have been manipulated

questions.passage: When I worked for a large electronics company that manufactured laser and ink-jet printers, I soon discovered why there are often three versions of many consumer goods. If the manufacturer makes only one version of its product, people who bought it might have been willing to spend more money, __________ the company is losing some income. If the company offers two versions, one with more features and more expensive than the other, people will compare the two models and still buy the less expensive one. But if the company introduces a third model with even more features and more expensive than the other two, sales of the second model go up; many people like the features of the most expensive model, but not the price. The middle item has more features than the least expensive one, and it is less expensive than the fanciest model. They buy the middle item, unaware that they have been manipulated by the presence of the higher-priced item.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: so=그래서 (사람들이 더 쓸 수 있었을 텐데, 그래서 회사는 수입을 잃는다는 결과)
det.analysis:
❌ ① because: because(~때문에)는 뒤에 원인이 와야 하나, 여기서는 결과가 이어짐
❌ ② unless: unless(~하지 않으면)는 조건의 의미로 맥락과 다름
✅ ③ so: 원문 일치. 사람들이 더 쓸 의향이 있었을 텐데, 그래서(so) 회사가 수입을 잃는다는 결과의 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ although: although(비록 ~이지만)는 양보의 의미로 결과 맥락과 다름
det.tip: 원인, so 결과: ~해서 그 결과 ~하다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: unaware=알지 못하는 (조종당한 것을 '알지 못한 채' 중간 제품을 산다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① certain: certain(확신하는)은 조종당한 줄 '모른다'는 맥락과 어긋남
❌ ② proud: proud(자랑스러운)는 속아서 산다는 맥락과 무관
❌ ③ aware: aware(알고 있는)는 '조종당한 줄 모른다'는 맥락과 정반대
✅ ④ unaware: 원문 일치. 소비자는 더 비싼 품목의 존재에 조종당한 줄 '알지 못한 채(unaware)' 중간 제품을 산다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: unaware that ~ = ~을 알지 못한 채
